stageA.product_summary: Rear combination lamp for M1 passenger cars. It integrates a rear position lamp, a stop lamp and a reversing lamp, all on non-replaceable LED modules on a PCB. It also has a red PMMA outer lens, an integral non-triangular red retro-reflector (Class IA/IB), a metallised PC reflector, an ASA/PC or PP housing, a gasket and fasteners. The lamp functions need device approval under R148 and the retro-reflector under R150. Installation must comply with R48, and the LED electronics bring in EMC requirements.

UN R10.how_it_applies: The rear lamp contains LED modules on a PCB with associated wiring and connector, so it is an electrical/electronic sub-assembly (ESA, para 2.8) that can be approved under UN R10 as a component or separate technical unit. Two of its functions, the stop lamp and the rear position lamp, are listed immunity-related functions (para 2.12), so the lamp must pass ESA immunity testing as well as the emission limits. Applicable requirements are: approval marking (para 5), broadband and narrowband radiated emission limits for ESAs (paras 6.5 and 6.6), radiated immunity of ESAs (para 6.8), and conducted transient immunity and emission on 12/24 V supply lines (Annex 10). The exceptions in para 6.10 may relieve some tests, depending on whether the electronics are active. Conformity of production (para 9) also applies. Because the light source is LED, the ESA-as-light-source provision (paras 3.2.10 / 4.2.4) applies: the lamp needs an R128 approval reference or a report that it is not mechanically interchangeable with approved light sources. The REESS charging-mode requirements (para 7) do not apply: the lamp is not part of a charging coupling system and has no AC/DC grid or network ports. Vehicle-level sections (6.2–6.4) concern the vehicle manufacturer, not this device. The lens, retro-reflector, housing, seal and fasteners are passive parts with no R10 obligations.

UN R148.how_it_applies: UN R148 type-approves light-signalling lamps regardless of light source technology. This rear combination lamp has three R148 functions in one housing: a rear position lamp (class R1 or R2), a stop lamp (class S1 or S2; not a central high-mounted stop lamp) and a reversing lamp (class AR). Each function needs its own approval symbol, though the lamp may carry a single grouped/combined approval mark. The outer lens, reflector, LED PCB and housing are parts of the lamp. They are assessed through the photometric, colour, visibility, vibration, light-source and failure provisions. The integrated retro-reflector is outside the R148 scope and falls under UN R150. Being grouped with it does not exempt the lamp functions, and the lamp may carry a combined mark with the R150 approval. A rear position lamp approved under R148 is also deemed approved as a rear end-outline marker lamp. EMC compliance is assessed at vehicle level (R10), not under R148.

UN R19.how_it_applies: UN R19 applies only to front fog lamps (Class B or F3) and to grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamps that include a front fog lamp. The product is a rear lamp for M1 vehicles. It combines a rear position lamp, a stop lamp, a reversing lamp and a rear retro-reflector behind a red outer lens. These functions fall under other regulations (R148, R150, R48), not R19. The product has no front fog lamp function, so R19 sets no obligations on it. Its plastic lens and LED provisions apply only within a front fog lamp approval.

UN R26.how_it_applies: UN R26 approves M1 vehicle types, not lamps, so the rear lamp carries no R26 approval or marking of its own. However, para 2.3 lists 'lighting and light-signalling devices' as part of the vehicle's external surface. Once installed on an M1 car, the lamp's exposed outer lens, any visible housing or bezel edges, and any exposed seal must meet the general external-projection requirements of para 5. These include no pointed or sharp parts, minimum radii of curvature, and the Shore A hardness provisions. Projection dimensions are measured with the Annex 3 methods, and the requirements carry into conformity of production. The headlight visor/rim provisions (6.2) do not apply because this is a rear lamp, not a headlamp. The other particular items (ornaments, grilles, bumpers, plate brackets, racks, aerials) are not functions of this product. The lamp's photometric, colour and retro-reflection performance is outside R26.

UN R48.how_it_applies: UN R48 approves the vehicle installation, not the lamp, so it applies indirectly. This rear combination lamp for M1 vehicles combines a rear position lamp, stop lamp, reversing lamp and non-triangular rear retro-reflector in one lamp body. Each function must be installable in compliance with R48. The lamp's photometric axis and apparent surfaces must allow the vehicle to meet the position, geometric-visibility and orientation requirements of paras 6.4, 6.7, 6.10 and 6.14. The colours must meet the R48 rules: red for position, stop and retro-reflector, white for reversing. The grouped or reciprocally incorporated combination must meet para 5.7. Electrical connections and any variable intensity control must suit para 5 and the individual function sections. Production lamps are checked under the visibility and intensity CoP (para 8 and Annex 9). The device itself still needs component approval under R148 (LSD) and R150 (RRD).

UN R53.how_it_applies: UN R53 is a vehicle installation regulation limited to category L3 (two-wheeled motorcycles). It sets the number, position, visibility, colour and switching of lamps fitted to an L3 vehicle. The product is a rear combination lamp specified for M1 passenger cars. Its installation is therefore governed by UN R48, and the device itself by the device regulations (R148 for the rear position, stop and reversing lamps, R150 for the retro-reflector). The inputs give no indication that the lamp is intended for an L3 motorcycle. R53 therefore places no obligations on this product. The functions present (rear position lamp, stop lamp, retro-reflector, grouped/combined layout) correspond to terms R53 defines, but only in an L3 vehicle context. The reversing lamp has no counterpart section in R53 at all. If the same lamp were ever offered for fitment to an L3 motorcycle, §5, §5.6, §5.20, §6.4, §6.7, §6.8, §8 and Annexes 3 and 4 would become relevant to that vehicle's installation approval.
